candidates.place_reason: 306d audit 2026-10-13: the 8 anchors are a 100-px grid ladder that is internally inconsistent (the 300-px square u 250-550 x v 450-750 spans 500 m at 1.667 m/px, but the 400-px v=600 row u 200..600 spans 800 m at 2.0 m/px - 1.2:1, the bury-castle class), so no similarity is trustworthy (LSQ 1.737 m/px, resid 5.9-52.9 m). The aerial confirms: the drawn keep (~290x180 m) sits on village housing ESE of the 1842 'Site of Castle' (next to 'Castleorchard'), and the drawn ring (~975x825 m) wraps the whole village at ~5x the real ~200 m earthworks; the plate's own geography is also wrong - its 'Duffield' label and 'To Duffield'/'To Belper' roads lie SOUTH of the ring, but the real town and the A535 run WEST of the castle. Document deleted.
candidates.why: line check: fabricated anchor pattern: 1D ladder (3 anchors share one coordinate, regular spacing on the other); grid-round page coordinates (9 of 9 distinct values on a 10-px grid); the gate's 19.6 m measures internal consistency of the anchors, not their truth
